subject: Security follow-up: subprocessor ownership & data flow clarifications
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Gomez <alice@cloudhealth.io>, b.park@axionpharm.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Security follow-up: subprocessor ownership & data flow clarifications

Hi Alice / B. Park — thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and open items from our call so we can keep procurement moving: 

1) SOC 2 status and evidence
   - Please confirm current SOC 2 Type (e.g., Type II) and whether an AOC (attestation) or interim report is available.
2) Applicable regulations
   - Clarify if HIPAA/PHI could be in scope for your use (you mentioned a small set of clinical identifiers).
3) Subprocessor ownership and cloud boundaries
   - We need a simple roster of the vendors that will process customer data (cloud providers, analytics, billing, monitoring). Please indicate which vendor stores or processes PII/PHI and whether Redwood is considered a subprocessor or data processor for each item.
4) Dataflow diagram request
   - A 1-page dataflow (high-level) showing where tokens, request logs, and artifacts are stored/processed. A Drive link or a simple diagram is fine.
5) Security questionnaire kickoff
   - We sent a short questionnaire link (see attachments). If you prefer, we can run through it in a call.

Owners & proposed deadlines:
- Alice: provide subprocessor roster + SOC2 AOC (by 2026-03-09)
- Karthik (internal): produce a draft dataflow and mapping to Redwood services (by 2026-03-10)
- Marissa (internal): review SOC2 evidence and list follow-ups (by 2026-03-11)

Attachments: cloudhealth-subprocessors.pdf (requested roster template), security-questionnaire-link.txt (one-click questionnaire).

Thanks — goal is to have the security Qs closed before legal routing.

Best,
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
log_wright@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Alice Gomez <alice@cloudhealth.io>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, b.park@axionpharm.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Security follow-up: subprocessor ownership & data flow clarifications

Hi Logan — thanks for the clear summary. Quick answers inline: 

- SOC 2: CloudHealth completed SOC 2 Type II for 2024-25. We can share the AOC under NDA; I attached the current subprocessor export and included a short note on our control scope.
- HIPAA: We are a business associate for a small number of customers; if Axion will send PHI we need to scope limited-data-handling and sign a BAA.
- Subprocessors (short list):
  * AWS (compute & storage) — us-east-1 (primary)
  * GCP (analytics & batch processing) — us-west2
  * S3-compatible archival via Backblaze B2 (long-term logs)
  * Segment (event routing) 
  * Stripe (billing)
  * Datadog (monitoring) — does not see raw documents (only metrics/traces)

I’ve attached cloudhealth-subprocessors.pdf and a spreadsheet roster. The roster marks which vendor touches PII/PHI. We don’t store raw PHI in the model prompts by default; any PHI flows into a redacted store (per our policy).

SOC2 AOC: happy to share after a simple mutual NDA or via a secure portal. What’s your procurement preference?

-Alice
Alice Gomez
Head of Security & Compliance | CloudHealth Systems
alice@cloudhealth.io | +1 (617) 555-2288

----
[Attachment: SUBPROCESSOR_ROSTER_v1.xlsx]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Gomez <alice@cloudhealth.io>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Security follow-up: subprocessor ownership & data flow clarifications

Thanks Alice — this is very helpful. A few clarifying asks so our Security & Legal teams can progress: 

1) SOC 2 evidence: is the AOC the full Type II attestation or an internal summary? If you can provide the AOC or a redacted copy (indicating control gaps if any), Legal will triage. Please point us to a secure upload (or we can accept via NDA portal).
2) BAA/HIPAA: if Axion expects any PHI transfer, please flag the specific data elements and the teams/paths that may touch PHI. We will treat that as a separate DPA/BAA conversation but need to know scope.
3) Data retention & encryption: could you confirm (a) encryption at rest for S3/Backblaze, (b) whether customer-managed keys (CMKs) are available for archival buckets, and (c) retention defaults for logs and prompts?
4) Subprocessor responsibilities: in the roster column please indicate whether CloudHealth (customer) or CloudHealth vendors (subprocessors) are responsible for access controls and deletion requests — that reduces ambiguity for cross-team ops.

Karthik — can you produce a one-page dataflow diagram mapping: Redwood request ingress -> CloudHealth processing -> where tokens/logs are stored -> which subprocessors see PII/PHI? Use the roster Alice provided as the starting point. Target EOD 2026-03-10.

Alice — if you can drop the AOC or a portal link, I’ll route to Legal and Security. If an NDA is required, we’ll send it today.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Product Security | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

I’ve also copied a one-click security questionnaire here for convenience: https://redwood.app/security/q/DEAL-8472 (short form that populates our vendor intake). If you’d rather have a live walkthrough, we can schedule 30 minutes this week.
